Unlike ray casting, it exploits cache coherency by sequentially traversing voxels, though it introduces low-pass filtering that blurs sharp boundaries [S1, unofficial][S6].

The claim is fully supported by the provided evidence. Source [S1] explicitly states that 'Splatting exploits cache coherency by sequentially traversing voxels in memory order, whereas ray casting requires random access.' It also notes that 'the generated images are blurred because of the spherically symmetric reconstruction kernel' and that 'Ray casting with trilinear reconstruction yields sharp object boundaries, unlike splatting.' Source [S6] corroborates the blurring aspect by stating that splatting 'introduces an additional low-pass filtering step... with the side effect that they perform some signal smoothing.' Thus, all parts of the claim (cache coherency via sequential traversal, low-pass filtering causing blur, and loss of sharp boundaries compared to ray casting) are present in the evidence.
